title: IBM style · Number series, English + Coding
description: Number series, English and a coding round. 22 MCQs + 2 coding problems in 95 minutes. Original practice questions modelled on the publicly reported test pattern. Not an official or past paper.

questions.text:
Read the passage and answer.

Electric vehicles are becoming more common in Indian cities. They produce no exhaust and are cheaper to run than petrol vehicles. Their main drawbacks are a higher purchase price and a shortage of charging stations. As battery prices fall and more chargers are installed, experts expect electric two-wheelers and buses to spread fastest.

Which vehicles are expected to spread fastest?
questions.explanation: The passage supports: Two-wheelers and buses.

questions.text: Fill in the blank: Please refrain ____ smoking here.
questions.explanation: Correct: Please refrain from smoking here.

questions.text:
Spot the part of the sentence that has an error:
(A) She is one of those (B) people who (C) always speaks (D) the truth.
questions.explanation: ‘who’ refers to ‘people’ (plural): ‘speak’.

questions.text: Choose the best replacement for the part in brackets: We [had a hard time to find] the hotel.
questions.explanation: Correct: We had a hard time finding the hotel.

questions.text:
Read the passage and answer.

Good sleep is essential for learning. While we sleep, the brain sorts and stores what we learned during the day. Students who stay up all night before an exam often remember less than those who sleep well, even if they studied for more hours. Regular sleep times, less screen use before bed and a dark, quiet room all improve sleep quality.

Which is NOT given as a way to improve sleep?
questions.explanation: The passage supports: Studying in bed.

questions.text: Fill in the blank: They were accused ____ cheating.
questions.explanation: Correct: They were accused of cheating.

questions.text:
Spot the part of the sentence that has an error:
(A) She is (B) the most (C) smartest girl (D) in the class.
questions.explanation: Double superlative: ‘the smartest girl’.

questions.text: Choose the best replacement for the part in brackets: She [laid] on the bed because she was tired.
questions.explanation: Correct: She lay on the bed because she was tired.

questions.text:
Read the passage and answer.

Many rivers in India are fed by Himalayan glaciers. As temperatures rise, these glaciers are shrinking. In the short term this can increase river flow and the risk of floods; in the long term, rivers may carry less water in dry months. Scientists stress the need to monitor glaciers and to plan water use carefully.

What is happening to Himalayan glaciers?
questions.explanation: The passage supports: They are shrinking.

questions.text: Fill in the blank: Do you know where ____?
questions.explanation: Correct: Do you know where she lives?

questions.title: Remove duplicates
questions.text:
Given n integers, print them with duplicates removed, keeping the first occurrence of each and the original order.

Input: first line n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5); second line n integers.
Output: the remaining numbers separated by spaces.

starterCode.python:
import sys

data = sys.stdin.read().split()
# write your code here
starterCode.javascript:
const data = require('fs').readFileSync(0, 'utf8').trim().split(/\s+/);
// write your code here

questions.explanation: Reference approach: see the standard technique for ‘Remove duplicates’.

questions.title: K-th largest element
questions.text:
Given n integers and k, print the k-th largest element (counting duplicates).

Input: first line n and k (1 ≤ k ≤ n ≤ 10^5); second line n integers.
Output: the k-th largest value.

starterCode.python:
import sys

data = sys.stdin.read().split()
# write your code here
starterCode.javascript:
const data = require('fs').readFileSync(0, 'utf8').trim().split(/\s+/);
// write your code here

questions.explanation: Reference approach: see the standard technique for ‘K-th largest element’.
